tasks.title: Feature doors land in a one-block vestibule that patrol flags door_to_wall
tasks.notes: Cause: feature_build lays storey floors every 3 blocks from a median-ground level but places each door on its own wall column's lidar ground, so the door's inside cell is floor or solid; 6 flags in the world after 2026-10-27 (jubilee 1, susu 3, west 2). Doors also fall back to one leaf when no pair cell is free (42-B, 57-A, 40-A/B, 18-A). Deliver: tie storey floors to local ground at each door, or clear the inside cell; then a re-apply of the three specs gives 0 patrol flags and keeps two-leaf doors where the spec asks for them. UPDATE 2026-10-27: this is the old door path that #146 removes, and #145 plans floor height against outside ground (the sunk 42-B door, I-017). Do not fix it twice: #146 absorbs the work, and this task is the acceptance check afterwards (re-apply the three specs: 0 patrol door_to_wall flags, two-leaf doors where the plan says double). Close it if #146 already gives that. Premature task/143-door-vestibule (ce1c96e) left unmerged: ticket says #146 absorbs the fix; branch kept for reference. Unblocked after #146: acceptance-only — fill facade_plan on live specs, re-apply, confirm 0 door_to_wall and leaf counts; close if #146 already satisfies. Discard premature task/143-door-vestibule branch.

tasks.title: Houses inside a larger footprint (39-47 University Road) reach the queue
tasks.notes: Fixes snag S-011 under the houses-dropping-out issue (I-012). Cause (verified read-only 2026-10-27): the houses (portals 1102-1107, x 6272-6300, z -5480..-5440) are in cell 49,-43, not 48,-44 (S-011 was tagged 48,-44 because the Jubilee build was there). They have no OSM footprint of their own: the vector map has one building=yes outline (Jubilee w93729745, 5192 columns) that swallows them. footprint_progress (lib/journal/cell_features.py) counts that outline as built (59% of columns covered, over COVERED_FRAC 0.5), and the Jubilee build excludes the houses on purpose, so no unbuilt row and no 'houses' candidate is ever produced; #140 and #142 cannot see them. Do: in footprint_progress / missing_features, when a footprint is judged built, still find portals inside it whose columns no feature build touches and emit them as an unbuilt 'houses' (or 'building') row with those portals, listed by propose-features and status for the owning cell. Add a test in lib/journal/test_cell_features.py with a footprint whose main part is covered and whose portal area is not. Re-check what undoing Jubilee does to coverage (unverified how touched_by_build treats undone builds). Correct S-011's cell to 49,-43. Not verified: whether the 3- and 4-house rows already listed for 49,-43 are other houses. Files: lib/journal/cell_features.py, its test, scripts/cell_registry.py only if the status output needs it. Check S-011: `python3 scripts/cell_registry.py --world southampton-build propose-features --cell 49,-43` lists a houses row on University Road covering portals 1102-1107; `status --cell 49,-43` shows it as unbuilt; `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_cell_features` passes.

tasks.title: Ground fills a pit its neighbours surround, instead of repainting the floor
tasks.notes: Fixes snag S-019 under the void-beside-walls issue (I-015). Cause (journal evidence 2026-10-27): a 3-wide diagonal band in the lidar ghost baseline (ghost_48_m44_ground: top y=36 against y=44 west and y=39 inside SUSU, about (6148,-5530) to (6144,-5514)) was hidden by the first SUSU build's stone fill (seq 52); undoing SUSU (seq 127) exposed the y=36 floor; the smaller rebuild (seq 138) starts at x=6148 so nothing refills the strip; ground reruns (seq 132, 188) repainted the floor in place. lib/layers/ground_layer.py plan_cell only sets the top at the live surface and raises only the one-block spike case (level_spikes), so ground never fills a pit. Not verified: why the baseline dips; live state beyond (6145-6147,-5520). Deliver: in ground_layer.py, detect a narrow pit among free columns (live surface lower than the surrounding non-pit level by at least a named threshold, about 3; not water, bank, bridge, steps, kerb or building footprint) and raise it to the surrounding outside-footprint level (44 here, not the 39 inside the building) with the right top block, using the existing raise fill. Guards: leave real cuttings, ponds, steps and underpasses (width limit, water/bridge skip). Decide in the task whether the baseline band is also fixed in the ghost; the ground fix is the general one. Test: MemoryBlocks fixture in lib/layers/test_ground_layer.py with a 3-wide 8-deep pit between level ground (filled, right top block) and one wide sunken area left unfilled. Check S-019: `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_ground_layer` passes; after a ground rerun on 48,-44 (site_lock run, redo ground) block_get_top_y at x 6145, 6146, 6147 on z -5520 equals x 6144 (44) with no air column y37-43, and the rest of the band z -5530..-5514 likewise. Files: lib/layers/ground_layer.py, lib/layers/test_ground_layer.py.
